A1.justification: Both PDFs describe StarVector, SVG-Stack, and SVG-Bench. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and matchable despite reflow and added discussion.

before.justification: V2 reports original image vectorization and text-to-SVG experiments, ablations, and a human evaluation comprising 1,948 judgments from 30 participants.

after.justification: V4 retains the original experiments, ablations, and human evaluation in Section 6 and Appendix 10.

M1.justification: The encoder–adapter–StarCoder architecture, two model variants, training objective, and SVG sampling and ranking procedures are retained. V4's suggestions for dynamic image processing and domain adaptation are future work, not implemented components.

E1.justification: The ten named SVG-Bench datasets and three tasks are retained. V4 additionally claims evaluations on datasets containing non-standard SVGs (appendix page 26), but neither identifies those datasets nor distinguishes them from existing benchmarks, preventing a reliable judgment about added coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding image vectorization, diagram, text-to-SVG, and ablation comparisons. V4 adds parameter-count descriptions for existing baselines; BeyondPixels is newly cited but not evaluated.

E3.justification: V4 newly reports a comparison between 4k and 10k token settings (appendix page 26), although the model, datasets, and precise control are unspecified. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and training settings are retained; the 8k dataset restriction was already documented in v2 Section 8.

E4.justification: V4 adds brief prose reports of context-length sensitivity and generalization assessment on non-standard SVGs, without accompanying quantitative breakdowns or identifiable test cases. Existing encoder, augmentation, pretraining, decoding, path-count, and primitive analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting practices are unchanged, including the human-evaluation Spearman analysis and dataset token-length dispersions. V4 introduces no new repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: V4 newly reports little score difference between 4k and 10k token settings and difficulty reproducing unfamiliar SVG styles. Existing numerical results are unchanged, including StarVector-8B's SVG-Stack DinoScore of 0.966 in Table 1; no same-setting performance improvement is reported.

T1.justification: The visual-token mapping, adapter equation, and conditional autoregressive formulation in Equations 1–3 are unchanged. Neither version contains additional theorems or proofs, and v4's new discussion is conceptual rather than mathematical.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about primitive-aware SVG generation, SVG-Stack, SVG-Bench, performance, and limitations of pixel-based evaluation. The central contribution and novelty claims are not substantively redefined.

C2.justification: Beyond v2's existing context, resolution, and data-scarcity limitations, v4 substantially expands qualifications concerning model-size imbalance, hallucinations attributed to noisy SVG content, and bias toward common styles. Appendix page 26 develops these applicability boundaries and proposed remedies, materially extending the interpretation of generalization and failure.

D1.justification: V4 adds approximate baseline parameter counts in Section 6, a project website address on the title page, and more explicit benchmark context-limit documentation. These are disclosure additions; the existing implementation, hardware, training-time, and hyperparameter descriptions are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds BeyondPixels as concurrent work using LLMs to predict synthetic SVG command sequences. This is a limited positioning update; the other cited works are retained, with VGBench merely renumbered from reference 99 to 100.

P1.justification: Several introduction, related-work, benchmark, and experimental paragraphs are condensed or edited. V4 also adds acknowledgements, updates affiliations, and inserts appendix discussion, while retaining the overall section sequence and narrative structure.

P2.justification: All ten tables and 31 figures are retained. Caption edits and reflow move Table 3 from page 7 to page 6 and regroup appendix figures around the added discussion; no new experimental display is introduced.

improvement.justification: V4 provides useful qualifications to the paper's broad generalization claims through discussion of model-size imbalance, unfamiliar SVG styles, and noisy data, while acknowledging relevant concurrent work. The core evidence is retained. However, its new context-length and non-standard-SVG evaluation statements lack sufficiently identified protocols and detailed outcomes, so the improvement is chiefly in transparency and positioning rather than empirical support.
